mainTopic: What a בעל קרי may say, Torah sources for blessings, and how doubts about קריאת שמע, אמת ויציב and תפלה are handled based on דאורייתא versus דרבנן.
overview: The amud opens by asking why a בעל קרי may think קריאת שמע and say ברכת המזון but may not begin תפלה. The answer is that קריאת שמע and ברכת המזון are דאורייתא, while תפלה is דרבנן. רב יהודה gives the Torah verses for ברכת המזון after eating and ברכת התורה before learning. רבי יוחנן tries to learn the missing blessings (after Torah study, before eating) by קל וחומר, but this is refuted. רב יהודה then rules that a doubt about קריאת שמע is not repeated but a doubt about אמת ויציב is, and the גמרא defends his view against challenges. רבי אלעזר disagrees and holds that קריאת שמע is repeated but תפלה is not, while רבי יוחנן says one should pray again. Finally, שמואל rules on someone who remembers mid-תפלה that he already prayed, and on praying again with a צבור. The explanation of why both of his rulings are needed continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from prayer: the community does it too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the reason a בעל קרי may think קריאת שמע is that the community is busy with it, then תפלה should be the same. Yet the rule is that a בעל קרי who has not started תפלה should not start it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about prayer? The community is also busy with it. And we learned: if someone was standing in prayer and remembered that he is a בעל קרי, he should not stop. Instead he should shorten it. The reason he continues is that he already started. If he had not started, he should not start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason given earlier, that a בעל קרי joins in so he is not idle while the community is busy. It points out that this reason should also apply to תפלה, but it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reason was 'the community is busy with it.' תפלה fits that description perfectly. Yet the source says a בעל קרי may only continue a תפלה he already began. From that the גמרא reads out a rule: he may not begin תפלה at all. So 'the community is busy with it' cannot be the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: But look at…: introduces a counter-example
One who had a seminal emission and has not yet immersed
The reason is X, which implies the opposite case: the classic inference formula

steps.confusionAlert: The source never says outright 'he should not begin.' The גמרא reads this out of the wording: the only reason he continues is that he already started.

phrases.english: But what about prayer,
which is a thing the community is busy with,
and we learned: if one was standing in prayer
and remembered that he is a בעל קרי,
he should not stop, but rather shorten it.
The reason is that he already began,
phrases.notes: This begins the inference.

phrases.english: but if he had not begun, he should not begin!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי תְּפִלָּה, דְּדָבָר שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר עֲסוּקִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier reason that a בעל קרי joins in because the community is busy with it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason 'דבר שהצבור עסוקין בו' as the explanation for why a בעל קרי thinks through קריאת שמע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תפלה also fits that reason, yet a בעל קרי may not begin it. So the reason cannot be correct.

steps.title: Prayer is different because it has no acceptance of God's kingship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תפלה is different: it contains no קבלת עול מלכות שמים, so it is less pressing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Prayer is different, because it does not contain the kingdom of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to save the earlier reason. It suggests that קריאת שמע is special because it contains accepting God's kingship, and תפלה does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new claim is narrower: what matters is not only that the community is busy with something, but that it contains מלכות שמים. קריאת שמע contains it, so he joins in. תפלה does not, so he does not begin.

keyTerms.meaning: Accepting the kingship of Heaven (as in the first פסוק of שמע)

phrases.english: Prayer is different
since it does not contain the kingdom of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the two cases differ in content (מלכות שמים).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that any community activity should be treated alike.
steps.terutzMaskana: קריאת שמע is special because of מלכות שמים, which תפלה lacks.

steps.title: Rejection from ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: The answer fails. ברכת המזון also has no מלכות שמים, yet a בעל קרי does say the blessing after eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: But ברכת המזון also does not contain מלכות שמים, and yet we learned: over food he blesses afterward but does not bless beforehand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from Step 2 with a counter-example: ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מלכות שמים were the deciding factor, a בעל קרי should not say ברכת המזון, since it lacks מלכות שמים. But the משנה says he does say the blessing after the meal. So מלכות שמים is not what separates the cases.

phrases.english: But what about Grace after Meals, said afterward,
which does not contain the kingdom of Heaven,
and we learned: over food he blesses afterward
but does not bless beforehand!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן לְאַחֲרָיו דְּלֵית בַּהּ מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that מלכות שמים is what decides the matter.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ברכת המזון lacks מלכות שמים, yet a בעל קרי still says it after eating.

steps.title: The real distinction: Torah law versus rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: The real difference is that קריאת שמע and ברכת המזון are Torah obligations, while תפלה is rabbinic. So a בעל קרי does not begin תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: קריאת שמע and ברכת המזון are from the Torah, and תפלה is rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The word 'אלא' signals that the גמרא drops the earlier attempts and gives the true explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither 'the community is busy with it' nor 'it has מלכות שמים' explains the cases. What does explain them is the source of the obligation. A בעל קרי still does Torah-level מצוות: he thinks קריאת שמע in his heart and says ברכת המזון after eating. תפלה, being rabbinic, is not begun in that state.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the previous idea and replaces it

steps.whatToRemember: A בעל קרי still does קריאת שמע and ברכת המזון because they are דאורייתא. He does not begin תפלה because it is דרבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This conclusion makes us ask whether ברכת המזון is really דאורייתא. That is why רב יהודה immediately brings its source.

phrases.english: Rather: the recitation of שמע and Grace after Meals
are from the Torah, and prayer is rabbinic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 2 with the final explanation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The source of the obligation (Torah or rabbinic) decides what a בעל קרי may say, not community involvement or מלכות שמים.

steps.title: Torah source for ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה brings the פסוק showing that ברכת המזון after eating is a Torah obligation: 'ואכלת ושבעת וברכת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: From where do we know that ברכת המזון, said afterward, is from the Torah? As it says: 'And you shall eat and be satisfied and bless.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the Torah verse behind the claim that ברכת המזון is דאורייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order in the פסוק matters: eat, be satisfied, then bless. That is why the Torah obligation is the blessing after the meal.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall eat and be satisfied and bless' (דברים ח:י)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לְבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן לְאַחֲרֶיהָ מִן הַתּוֹרָה —
phrases.english: From where is Grace after Meals, after eating, from the Torah?
As it says: 'And you shall eat and be satisfied and bless.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: מִנַּיִן לְבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן לְאַחֲרֶיהָ מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the Torah source for the claim in Step 4 that ברכת המזון is דאורייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת המזון after eating is a Torah obligation, learned from 'ואכלת ושבעת וברכת'.

steps.title: Torah source for the blessing before Torah study
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה continues: ברכת התורה before learning is also from the Torah, learned from 'כי שם ה׳ אקרא הבו גדל לאלהינו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that the blessing over the Torah, said beforehand, is from the Torah? As it says: 'When I call the name of ה׳, give greatness to our God.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה, still speaking, adds a second Torah-level blessing, ברכת התורה, together with its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the blessing comes before the act. When one 'calls God's name' by reading Torah, he must first 'give greatness,' meaning bless God. This is the reverse of ברכת המזון, which comes after eating.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When I call the name of ה׳‎' (דברים לב:ג)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two Torah-level blessings: ברכת המזון comes after eating, and ברכת התורה comes before learning.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the timing. ברכת המזון is after (לאחריה), while ברכת התורה is before (לפניה).

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לְבִרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה לְפָנֶיהָ מִן הַתּוֹרָה —
phrases.english: From where is the blessing over the Torah, before it, from the Torah?
As it says: 'When I call the name of ה׳,'
'give greatness to our God.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לְבִרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה לְפָנֶיהָ מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יהודה's statement with a second Torah-level blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת התורה before learning is a Torah obligation, learned from 'כי שם ה׳ אקרא הבו גדל לאלהינו'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's Headline: Two Blessings Learned by Logic
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says two blessings are learned by קל וחומר. The blessing after Torah learning comes from ברכת המזון, and the blessing before eating comes from ברכת התורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: We learned that there is a blessing after Torah study from ברכת המזון, using a קל וחומר. And we learned that there is a blessing before eating from ברכת התורה, using a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן states his claim in short form. The next two steps will spell out each argument in detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah gives us only one blessing for each activity. For food, it gives the blessing after eating (ואכלת ושבעת וברכת). For Torah, it gives the blessing before learning (כי שם ה׳ אקרא). רבי יוחנן wants each one to 'borrow' the missing blessing from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument 'from the lighter case to the stricter case': if the weaker case has a rule, the stronger case surely has it too

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
We learned the blessing of the Torah afterward
from Grace after Meals, by an a fortiori argument,
and the blessing over food beforehand
from the blessing of the Torah, by an a fortiori argument.
phrases.notes: Each blessing 'lends' its missing half to the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of Torah-level blessings from רב יהודה's two פסוקים. It tries to add two more blessings by logic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blessing after Torah study and a blessing before eating are both derived by קל וחומר.

steps.title: First Argument: Blessing After Torah Study
steps.stepSummary: Food needs no blessing before it, yet it needs one after it. So Torah, which needs a blessing before, surely needs one after.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is how we learn the blessing after Torah from ברכת המזון: Food does not need a blessing before it, but it does need one after it. Torah does need a blessing before it. Isn't it logical that it also needs one after it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן spells out his first קל וחומר. It shows that Torah study should need a blessing afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that Torah is 'stronger' than food when it comes to blessings, because it already needs a blessing beforehand. If the 'weaker' item, food, still gets a blessing afterward, the stronger one should too.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not logical? (the standard phrase that ends a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: The blessing of the Torah afterward
from Grace after Meals, by an a fortiori argument:
If food, which does not require a blessing before it,
requires one after it,
then Torah, which requires a blessing before it,
is it not logical that it requires one after it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first half of the headline in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By קל וחומר from food, Torah study needs a blessing afterward.

steps.title: Second Argument: Blessing Before Eating
steps.stepSummary: Torah needs no blessing after it, yet it needs one before it. So food, which needs a blessing after, surely needs one before.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here is how we learn the blessing before food from ברכת התורה: Torah does not need a blessing after it, but it does need one before it. Food does need a blessing after it. Isn't it logical that it also needs one before it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן spells out the mirror-image argument. This one shows that eating should need a blessing beforehand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same logic as step 8 but turned around. Here food is the 'stronger' case, because it already has the blessing afterward.

phrases.english: And the blessing over food beforehand
from the blessing of the Torah, by an a fortiori argument:
If Torah, which does not require a blessing after it,
requires one before it,
then food, which requires a blessing after it,
is it not logical that it should require one before it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the second half of the headline in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By קל וחומר from Torah, food needs a blessing beforehand.

steps.title: Both Arguments Can Be Broken
steps.stepSummary: Food is special because a person enjoys it. Torah is special because it gives eternal life. So neither one can teach about the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted. Food is special because a person gets pleasure from it. And Torah is special because it gives eternal life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in each קל וחומר. It shows that food and Torah each have a unique quality that the other lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the 'teaching' case has no special feature of its own. Food gets a blessing afterward perhaps only because of the physical pleasure of eating, and Torah has no such pleasure. Torah gets a blessing beforehand perhaps only because it gives eternal life, and food does not.

keyTerms.meaning: What about X, which has this special feature? (standard form for breaking a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: One can refute this:
What about food? It is special because one benefits from it.
phrases.notes: This breaks the argument in step 8.

phrases.english: And what about Torah? It is special because it is eternal life.
phrases.notes: This breaks the argument in step 9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks both קל וחומר arguments from steps 8 and 9.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each 'teaching' case has a unique feature (pleasure or eternal life) that could explain its blessing, so the comparison does not hold.

steps.title: The משנה Contradicts Him: Final Refutation
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה says that for food, a בעל קרי blesses after but not before. That fits poorly with a Torah-level blessing before food, so רבי יוחנן is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, we learned in the משנה: Over food he blesses afterward but does not bless beforehand. This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger attack from our own משנה. It then declares רבי יוחנן's view conclusively refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 taught that a בעל קרי still says blessings that are Torah-level. If the blessing before food were Torah-level by קל וחומר, the משנה should let the בעל קרי say it. Since the משנה says he does not, the blessing before food must be only rabbinic, and רבי יוחנן's קל וחומר fails.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation: the view is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's two קל וחומר arguments are rejected. Only ברכת המזון afterward and ברכת התורה beforehand are Torah-level. The blessing before eating is rabbinic.

phrases.english: And furthermore, we learned in the Mishnah:
Over food he blesses afterward
phrases.notes: This refers to the בעל קרי in our משנה.

phrases.english: but does not bless beforehand.
This is a conclusive refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, תְּנַן עַל הַמָּזוֹן מְבָרֵךְ לְאַחֲרָיו וְאֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second attack, this time from a משנה, and closes the discussion with תיובתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the blessing before food is Torah-level by קל וחומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A בעל קרי says Torah-level blessings. The משנה says he skips the blessing before food, so that blessing is not Torah-level.

steps.title: רב יהודה: Unsure About קריאת שמע Versus Unsure About אמת ויציב
steps.stepSummary: If you are unsure whether you said קריאת שמע, you do not repeat it. If you are unsure whether you said אמת ויציב, you do repeat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: If a person is unsure whether he said קריאת שמע, he does not go back and say it. If he is unsure whether he said אמת ויציב, he goes back and says אמת ויציב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling from רב יהודה about what to do when in doubt. It is still connected to the theme of Torah-level versus rabbinic obligations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling seems backwards at first: the main part (שמע) is not repeated, while the blessing after it (אמת ויציב) is repeated. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing after the morning שמע, which mentions leaving Egypt

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק קָרָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, סָפֵק לֹא קָרָא —
phrases.english: If he is unsure whether he recited Shema or did not recite it,
he does not go back and recite it.

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק אָמַר ״אֱמֶת וְיַצִּיב״, סָפֵק לֹא אָמַר —
phrases.english: If he is unsure whether he said 'Emet VeYatziv' or did not say it,
he goes back and says 'Emet VeYatziv'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: סָפֵק קָרָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ruling that uses the same Torah-versus-rabbinic idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In doubt, one does not repeat קריאת שמע but does repeat אמת ויציב.

steps.title: The Reason: קריאת שמע Is Rabbinic, אמת ויציב Is Torah-Level
steps.stepSummary: קריאת שמע is rabbinic, so in doubt we are lenient. אמת ויציב, which mentions leaving Egypt, is from the Torah, so in doubt we are strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? קריאת שמע is rabbinic. אמת ויציב is from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב יהודה's ruling and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a doubt about a rabbinic law is treated leniently (ספק דרבנן לקולא), and a doubt about a Torah law is treated strictly (ספק דאורייתא לחומרא). אמת ויציב fulfills the Torah מצוה of remembering the Exodus (זכירת יציאת מצרים), so it is Torah-level.
steps.confusionAlert: In step 4 the גמרא treated קריאת שמע as a Torah obligation. Here רב יהודה holds it is only rabbinic. This is his own view, and the next step immediately challenges it.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Shema is rabbinic.
phrases.notes: A rabbinic doubt is treated leniently.

phrases.english: 'Emet VeYatziv' is from the Torah.
phrases.notes: It is the Torah מצוה of remembering the Exodus, so a doubt is treated strictly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב יהודה's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is אמת ויציב repeated but שמע is not?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמע is rabbinic, so a doubt is lenient. אמת ויציב is Torah-level, so a doubt is strict.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The Torah Itself Says 'When You Lie Down and When You Rise'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges the idea that שמע is rabbinic, quoting the פסוק 'ובשכבך ובקומך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: But the Torah says, 'when you lie down and when you rise'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רב יהודה's claim that קריאת שמע is only rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in the first paragraph of שמע seems to command saying these words at night and in the morning. That would make קריאת שמע a Torah obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: When you lie down and when you rise (דברים ו:ז)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection:
'When you lie down and when you rise'!
phrases.notes: This seems to be a Torah command to say שמע at night and in the morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that קריאת שמע is דרבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah explicitly says 'when you lie down and when you rise', which implies a Torah-level obligation to recite שמע.

steps.title: אביי: That Verse Is About Learning Torah
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the פסוק refers to learning Torah in general, not specifically to reciting שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: That verse was written about words of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רב יהודה. He reads the פסוק as a general command to learn Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ודברת בם... ובשכבך ובקומך' can mean 'speak words of Torah at all times', not 'recite these specific paragraphs'. Read that way, the פסוק does not create a Torah obligation of קריאת שמע, and רב יהודה's view stands.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יהודה, as defended by אביי, a doubt about שמע is not repeated because שמע is rabbinic. A doubt about אמת ויציב is repeated because remembering the Exodus is a Torah מצוה.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
That verse was written about words of Torah.
phrases.notes: It is a general command to learn Torah, not specifically to recite שמע.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הָהוּא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק 'ובשכבך ובקומך' commands reciting שמע, so שמע is Torah-level.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק commands Torah study in general, so רב יהודה can hold that קריאת שמע is rabbinic.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about a בעל קרי and blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings our משנה as the source for an attempted proof about whether אמת ויציב is from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: a בעל קרי thinks the words of שמע in his heart. He does not say the blessing before it or the blessing after it. But for food, he says the blessing after eating, though not the blessing before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof by quoting our משנה. The actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the two cases differently. For שמע, the בעל קרי skips the blessing after it, which is אמת ויציב. For food, he says the blessing after it, which is ברכת המזון, a Torah requirement. The גמרא will use this difference to argue about the status of אמת ויציב.

keyTerms.meaning: Thinks the words in his heart without saying them aloud
After it (the blessing after שמע, which is אמת ויציב)

phrases.english: We learned: one who had a seminal emission thinks [שמע] in his heart
phrases.notes: This is our משנה.

phrases.english: and he does not bless, neither before it
phrases.notes: Before it means the blessings before שמע.

phrases.english: nor after it.
phrases.notes: After it means אמת ויציב. This is the key detail.

phrases.english: And over food, he blesses after it
phrases.notes: ברכת המזון is from the Torah.

phrases.english: but does not bless before it.
phrases.notes: The blessing before food is only rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to test the claim from step 13 that אמת ויציב is from the Torah.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the obligation of אמת ויציב is from the Torah.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: a בעל קרי skips the blessing after שמע but says the blessing after food.

steps.title: If אמת ויציב were from the Torah, he should say it
steps.stepSummary: The בעל קרי skips the blessing after שמע. So it seems אמת ויציב is not from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think אמת ויציב is from the Torah, then he should say the blessing after שמע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the משנה. It challenges the idea that אמת ויציב is a Torah requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With food, the בעל קרי says the after-blessing because it is from the Torah. If אמת ויציב were also from the Torah, he should say it too. Since the משנה says he skips it, it seems to be only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you think (if it enters your mind)

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
phrases.notes: Standard opening for a challenge.

phrases.english: that אמת ויציב is from the Torah —
phrases.notes: This was the claim in step 13.

phrases.english: let him say the blessing after it!
phrases.notes: Just as he does with ברכת המזון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the משנה quoted in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 13's claim that אמת ויציב is from the Torah.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Torah-level after-blessings, like ברכת המזון, are said even by a בעל קרי. The משנה says he skips the blessing after שמע. So that blessing must not be from the Torah.

steps.title: He already mentioned leaving Egypt in שמע
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The Torah only requires mentioning יציאת מצרים, and the בעל קרי already did that in שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does a person say אמת ויציב? If it is to mention leaving Egypt, he already mentioned it in קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It explains why the בעל קרי can skip אמת ויציב even if there is a Torah requirement behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah requirement is to mention יציאת מצרים. It is not a requirement to say the exact words of אמת ויציב. The last paragraph of שמע, about ציצית, already mentions leaving Egypt. So when he thinks שמע in his heart, the Torah requirement is covered, and skipping אמת ויציב loses nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not say that mentioning יציאת מצרים is rabbinic. It says the Torah requirement was already fulfilled through שמע. That is why skipping אמת ויציב proves nothing.

phrases.english: What is the reason he says it [אמת ויציב]?
phrases.notes: Asking what the Torah requirement really is.

phrases.english: If it is because of leaving Egypt —
phrases.notes: This is the Torah-level element.

phrases.english: he already mentioned it in קריאת שמע.
phrases.notes: In the paragraph about ציצית, which ends with leaving Egypt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה. It does not decide the status of אמת ויציב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes that skipping אמת ויציב means skipping a Torah requirement. But that requirement (mentioning leaving Egypt) was already met in שמע.

steps.title: Why not say אמת ויציב instead of שמע?
steps.stepSummary: If both mention leaving Egypt, why not say אמת ויציב and skip שמע?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him say this one (אמת ויציב) and not need that one (שמע)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up challenge on the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said that שמע covers the mention of leaving Egypt. But אמת ויציב also covers it. So why should the בעל קרי think שמע rather than אמת ויציב? Either one should work.

phrases.english: Let him say this one, and not need that one!
phrases.notes: The first "this" is אמת ויציב. The second "that" is שמע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to use שמע for mentioning leaving Egypt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both texts mention leaving Egypt, they should be interchangeable. So שמע should not be preferred.

steps.title: שמע is better because it has two things
steps.stepSummary: שמע is preferred because it has two elements: accepting God as King and mentioning leaving Egypt.
steps.simpleTranslation: קריאת שמע is better, because it contains two things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains why שמע is the better choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמת ויציב mostly contains the mention of leaving Egypt. שמע contains that and also קבלת עול מלכות שמים, accepting God as King. Since one text covers two things, it is chosen over the text that covers only one.

keyTerms.meaning: Accepting God as King (the second element in שמע)

steps.whatToRemember: The proof that אמת ויציב is rabbinic was rejected. The בעל קרי skips it because שמע already covers leaving Egypt. שמע is preferred because it has two elements.

phrases.english: קריאת שמע is preferable,
phrases.notes: Answers step 19.

phrases.english: because it has two [elements] in it.
phrases.notes: The two elements are accepting God as King and mentioning leaving Egypt.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע עֲדִיפָא, דְּאִית בַּהּ תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a reason for preferring one text over the other.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both texts mention leaving Egypt, they seem equal.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמע has two elements, so it is preferred.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: In doubt, repeat קריאת שמע but not תפלה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that a person who is unsure whether he said קריאת שמע must say it again. A person who is unsure whether he davened does not daven again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: If someone is not sure whether he said קריאת שמע, he goes back and says קריאת שמע. If he is not sure whether he davened, he does not go back and daven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new opinion from רבי אלעזר about what to do when a person is unsure whether he did a מצוה. He treats קריאת שמע and תפלה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the difference is the source of each obligation. קריאת שמע is from the Torah (דאורייתא), so a doubt about it is treated strictly. תפלה is from the Rabbis (דרבנן), so a doubt about it is treated leniently.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes back and reads (says it again)
A doubt about a Torah law is treated strictly (the principle behind this ruling)
A doubt about a Rabbinic law is treated leniently

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves. In רבי אלעזר's view, קריאת שמע IS repeated and תפלה is NOT. It is the opposite of what some people expect, since תפלה feels more 'serious'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic halachic pattern: how we act in a doubt depends on whether the obligation is דאורייתא or דרבנן.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק קָרָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע סָפֵק לֹא קָרָא —
phrases.english: If he is unsure whether he read Shema or did not read it,
phrases.notes: A real doubt, with no way to clarify.

phrases.english: he goes back and reads Shema.
phrases.notes: Strict, because קריאת שמע is from the Torah.

phrases.english: If he is unsure whether he prayed or did not pray,
he does not go back and pray.
phrases.notes: Lenient, because תפלה is Rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רב יהודה (steps 12–13). רב יהודה held that a doubt about קריאת שמע is not repeated because it is דרבנן. רבי אלעזר holds that it is repeated because it is דאורייתא, and he adds that a doubt about תפלה, which is דרבנן, is not repeated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubt about קריאת שמע requires repeating it (it is דאורייתא). A doubt about תפלה does not require repeating it (it is דרבנן).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: If only a person would pray all day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees about תפלה. He says that someone in doubt should daven again, because it would be wonderful if a person davened the whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: If only a person would pray the entire day!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with the second half of רבי אלעזר's ruling. He holds that someone unsure whether he davened should daven again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's point is that an extra תפלה is never a waste. If he already davened, the second one simply counts as a voluntary prayer (תפלת נדבה). So there is no reason to hold back when in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: If only; it would be wonderful if
A voluntary extra prayer (the idea behind רבי יוחנן's view)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying a person must daven all day. He is saying that extra davening is so good that, when in doubt, you should daven again.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
If only a person would pray
the entire day!
phrases.notes: So in a doubt, he should pray again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the second half of רבי אלעזר's ruling, the part about a doubt in תפלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone unsure whether he davened should daven again, since extra תפלה is always good.

steps.title: שמואל: If you remember mid-תפלה that you already prayed, stop immediately
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: if someone is in the middle of davening and remembers that he already davened, he stops, even in the middle of a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If someone was standing in תפלה and remembered that he had already davened, he stops, even in the middle of a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about a person who discovers, in the middle of davening, that he already davened. He must stop right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he already fulfilled his obligation, the current תפלה is not needed, so he does not even finish the ברכה he is in. This is the ruling the גמרא will challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing in prayer (in the middle of שמונה עשרה)
In the middle of a blessing

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If he was standing in prayer
and remembered that he had already prayed, he stops,
even in the middle of a blessing.
phrases.notes: This is the point that will be challenged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a doubt about davening to a person who becomes certain, in the middle of davening, that he already davened.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who remembers mid-תפלה that he already davened must stop at once, even in the middle of a ברכה.

steps.title: Challenge: On שבת, a mistaken weekday blessing must be finished
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל using רבה בר אבוה's ruling that students who wrongly started a weekday ברכה on שבת must finish that whole ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? Didn't רב נחמן say: When we were in the yeshiva of רבה בר אבוה, we asked him: Students who make a mistake and say a weekday ברכה on שבת, should they finish it? And he told us: They finish that entire ברכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions שמואל's rule by pointing to a case where someone said a ברכה by mistake and was still told to finish it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת we only say seven ברכות, so a weekday ברכה is said in error, yet רבה בר אבוה ruled that the person finishes it. If a mistaken ברכה must be finished there, why does שמואל say to stop in the middle of a ברכה here?

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rav Nachman say:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: When we were in the school of Rabba bar Avuh,
we asked him:
These yeshiva students
who mistakenly mention the weekday [prayer] on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: They began a weekday ברכה in the שבת שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: should they finish it?
And he told us:
They finish that entire blessing!
phrases.notes: This seems to contradict stopping in the middle of a ברכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's ruling from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that one stops even in the middle of a ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברכה said by mistake on שבת must be finished. So a ברכה begun by mistake should also be finished in שמואל's case.

steps.title: Answer: On שבת he is truly obligated; here he already prayed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. On שבת the person really is obligated in all the weekday ברכות, and the Rabbis only spared him because of שבת. Here he already davened, so he has no obligation at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them! There, the man is obligated, and it is only the Rabbis who did not trouble him, out of respect for שבת. But here, he already davened!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the two cases are different, so שמואל's rule stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת the weekday ברכות are really appropriate, and the Rabbis only shortened the davening out of כבוד שבת, so a weekday ברכה is not totally out of place and he may finish it. In שמואל's case he already fulfilled his תפלה, so the ברכה has no basis at all and he stops immediately.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: Finishing a mistaken ברכה depends on whether the person has any real obligation. On שבת he does, so he finishes the ברכה. After already davening he does not, so he stops even mid-ברכה.

phrases.english: How can you compare!
There, the man is one who is obligated,
phrases.notes: On שבת, the full weekday davening is fitting in principle.

phrases.english: and it is the Rabbis who did not burden him
because of the honor of Shabbat,
but here — he already prayed!
phrases.notes: No obligation remains, so he stops.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24 by distinguishing the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any ברכה started by mistake must be finished, as on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only someone with a real underlying obligation finishes the ברכה. Someone who already davened stops immediately.

steps.title: שמואל: Praying again with a congregation only if you add something new
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: a person who already davened and enters a shul where the צבור is davening may daven again only if he can add something new to his תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If a person already davened and then entered a בית הכנסת and found the צבור davening, if he can add something new to it, he may daven again. If not, he should not daven again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling of שמואל about davening a second time. It is allowed only if the extra תפלה includes something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A second תפלה is a voluntary prayer, and it must not look like a pointless copy of the first. Adding a new request or phrase makes it a real, fresh prayer. Without anything new, he does not repeat it.

keyTerms.meaning: To add something new to it
He may go back and pray again

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If he prayed and then entered a synagogue
and found a congregation praying,
if he can add something new to it,
phrases.notes: A new request or phrase in the תפלה.

phrases.english: he may pray again,
and if not, he should not pray again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling of שמואל on davening twice. This time the person chooses to daven again, rather than discovering it by mistake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who already davened may daven again with the צבור only if he adds something new to his תפלה.

steps.title: Both of שמואל's rulings are needed: the first might apply only to a lone person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why שמואל needed to say both rulings. Had we heard only the first one, we might have limited it to a lone person davening a second time on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both rulings are needed. If שמואל had taught us only the first one, we would have said: that applies only when one individual davened, and then that same individual davens again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to explain why שמואל's two similar rulings are both needed, so that neither one is extra. This step is only the first half of that explanation. It sets up the next move, which will show what the second ruling adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a hidden question here: why would שמואל say the same idea twice? The answer starts like this. The first ruling (step 23, stopping in the middle of davening) might have been limited to a person davening alone. That would leave open the idea that joining a צבור is different and lets him daven again freely. The second ruling (step 26, entering a shul) is about exactly that case, so it is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is necessary.' The opening word of a צריכותא, which explains why two similar teachings are both needed.
The גמרא's method of showing that each of two similar statements teaches something new.
'The first one.' Here it means שמואל's earlier ruling.
'These words apply.' It means 'this applies only to...' and limits a ruling to a narrower case.
An individual davening alone, not together with a צבור.

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase יחיד ויחיד does not mean two different people. It means the person was a יחיד both times: he davened alone the first time and is davening alone again. The contrast that is coming is a person who davened alone and then finds a צבור davening.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows that the second ruling is not repetition. It tells us that even a צבור does not automatically let someone daven a second time. He may do so only if he adds something new.

phrases.english: And it is necessary (to state both rulings),
phrases.notes: This opens the צריכותא and answers the unspoken question of why שמואל repeated himself.

phrases.english: for if he had taught us only the first one,
phrases.notes: The 'first one' is the ruling that someone who remembers he already davened stops, even in the middle of a ברכה.

phrases.english: (we would say) that applies only to an individual and an individual,
phrases.notes: In other words, he davened alone and then davens again alone. This passage ends here, and the second half of the צריכותא continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 26 gave שמואל's second ruling, which looks like a repeat of his first. This step begins explaining why both are needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each statement covers a case the other might not cover
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the first ruling alone, one might think it is limited to a lone person davening again alone. Then joining a צבור might allow a second תפלה freely.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet fully stated on this amud. The second ruling teaches that even with a צבור, he may daven again only if he adds something new.
